analysis.title: Prime Insights & Analytics Chart Pack, October 2026
key_insights: Goldman's Prime Services desk says October has tested the AI trade. A hotter-than-expected US CPI print and renewed doubts over the payoff from heavy AI capex sparked a sharp unwind in semis and AI infrastructure names that began in Asian memory stocks.
Global Fundamental L/S funds are down -2.5% in October through 10/19 (+10.1% YTD), driven by both alpha and beta losses. They finished September at -0.55%.
TMT L/S funds are down -7.4% MTD (+10.2% YTD) and Asia L/S funds are down -6.3% MTD (+17.1% YTD). Systematic L/S funds are up +0.65% MTD and +20.5% YTD.

Hedge funds heavily net sold global equities MTD, with short sales outpacing long buys by about 5 to 1. Long leverage is in the 73rd percentile vs. the past year (94th percentile 5-year). Short leverage is in the 99th percentile, approaching 5-year highs, and the desk flags short squeeze risk.
Fundamental L/S net leverage fell -3.1 pts MTD to 49.4% (1st percentile 1-year, 4th percentile 3-year). Gross leverage rose +5.4 pts to 211.9% (66th percentile 1-year, 89th percentile 3-year).

Beta adjusted Fundamental L/S net leverage fell -8.7 pts during Oct 12-16 (-3.8 SDs 5-year) and -10.9 pts month/month, one of the sharpest declines in the desk's data. It is still higher in absolute and percentile terms than the unadjusted measure.
All major regions except Europe (modestly net bought) are net sold MTD, led by North America (short sales far outpacing long buys) and EM Asia (short and long sales).

Within Asia, Taiwan, Japan and Korea are the most net sold markets in dollar terms MTD, while Australia and Hong Kong are the most net bought. Net allocation to Korea is 3.3%, down from a peak of about 8% in June and the lowest since early February.

Global Info Tech had the largest 2-week % net selling (Oct 5-16) on record, over 10+ years (-3.3 SDs), driven by long and short sales. Net allocation to Global AI stocks (GSXGGLAI) is in the 38th percentile and the aggregate long/short ratio is in the 6th percentile vs. the past year.

Mag 7 net allocation has risen to a new record high and net flows in mega cap tech were resilient over the past month. The gap between US Semis & Semi Equip and Software net exposures continues to narrow.

The US Cyclicals (GSXUCYCL) long/short ratio is in the 5th percentile, approaching 3-year lows, which the desk reads as growing caution on the growth outlook. Consumer Disc, Materials, Energy and Financials are among the most net sold sectors MTD, while Health Care, Real Estate and Staples are among the most net bought.

Consumer Disc is net sold MTD, driven by short sales, while Staples is net bought, driven by short covers. Hotels, Restaurants & Leisure, Broadline Retail and Household Durables are among the most net sold subsectors.

HFs have unwound Health Care risk for 5 consecutive weeks, led by de-grossing in Biotech since mid-August. The desk says this looks to be in the late innings, as flows moved from long sales to short covers and the pace has started to moderate.

Net exposure to Medium-Term Momentum is on track to fall for a 5th straight month to the lowest since Jun '25 (73rd percentile 5-year). Net exposure to Profitability has risen sharply to 5-year highs as managers move toward higher quality names.

Fundamental L/S alpha is down -1.4% MTD (+6.9% YTD), driven by long side losses. Asset Selection, Momentum, Volatility and Info Tech are the largest detractors, partly offset by gains in Consumer Disc, Dividend Yield and Long Crowdedness.
